# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 63 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_063_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 63

**1** Jesus said: "There was a rich man who had much money. He said: 'I will put my money to use so that I may sow, reap, plant, and fill my storehouses with produce, that I will lack nothing.'

**2** These were the things he was thinking in his heart.

**3** And that night he died.

**4** Whoever has ears, let him hear."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Thomas's version is strikingly brief compared to Luke 12:16-21. There is no divine address ("Fool!"), no "soul" dialogue, no "so it is for one who stores up for himself." The death alone is the answer.

**"Storehouses"** — EMET preferred over "barns" (LOGOS) — the Coptic does not use a farm-specific word; storehouses is slightly broader.

**"These were the things he was thinking in his heart"** — EMET's rendering retained for its Semitic idiom — "heart" as seat of thought is preserved.

**"Put my money to use"** — EMET/PNEUMA preferred over "invest" (LOGOS) — investment is anachronistic; the Coptic suggests deploying capital in agricultural production.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Luke 12:16-21 (the Rich Fool). Thomas strips the parable to its narrative essentials: ambition, death, silence. The closing formula "Whoever has ears, let him hear" signals parabolic interpretation required.
